title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 1
statement: Alicia had two containers. The first was \(\frac{5}{6}\) full of water and the second was empty. She poured all the water from the first container into the second container, at which point the second container was \(\frac{3}{4}\) full of water. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller container to the volume of the larger container?

solutions.text:
Let the volumes of the first and second containers be \(F\) and \(S\). The amount of water is both \(\dfrac56F\) and \(\dfrac34S\), so \(\dfrac56F=\dfrac34S\).

Thus \(\dfrac{F}{S}=\dfrac{\frac{3}{4}}{\frac{5}{6}}=\dfrac9{10}\). Since the first container is smaller, the ratio of the smaller container to the larger container is \(\dfrac9{10}\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the container volumes be variables
Equate the same water amount before and after pouring
